Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-10

Attendees: Samir (AE), Leah (SE) - Redwood; Dana (Head of Data), Miguel (ML Eng), Priya (Security) - HelioHealth

Summary (auto):
- Discovery call focused on embeddings and reranking for HelioHealth's medical search product.
- Discussed embedding dimensionality, vector DB choices, hybrid search with BM25 + ANN, rerank plan with a cross-encoder, and deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Next steps: pricing, benchmark runbook, SOC2/security pack, schedule POC kickoff.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood, account lead, and with me is Leah from our solutions engineering team. How are you all?
[00:06] Dana: Hi, thanks. Dana here, head of data at HelioHealth. We're excited to talk through embeddings and reranking.
[00:10] Miguel: Miguel, ML eng. We've been prototyping with Pinecone but hitting some cost and latency tradeoffs.
[00:15] Priya: Priya, security. I'll mostly listen but will ask compliance questions as we go.
[00:18] Samir: Great. Quick agenda: understand current stack and pain points, talk embedding dims and vector DB options, discuss throughput/latency SLOs, and then deployment/security constraints.
[00:27] Leah: Nice to meet you all. A little context on Redwood: we offer hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC/on-prem options. For embeddings and rerank we're seeing folks do dense retrieval for recall and then a small cross-encoder rerank on the top-K. We'll talk about how that maps to throughput and cost.
[00:42] Dana: Our use case: internal clinical search across patient notes and published literature. Sensitive data, so Priya's here for the compliance side. We have roughly 12M docs, average doc embedding count about 1.2 per doc (we chunk), so ~14M vectors.
[00:55] Miguel: Query volume currently ~150 qps peak for search API, but for some reports we need burst to 300 qps. Latency P95 target is 200ms end-to-end for the initial retrieval, rerank allowed to add another 100-200ms depending on batch.
[01:12] Leah: Good, those are helpful numbers. A couple immediate flags: 14M vectors is modest for production, but cost and topology depend on vector dim and ANN index type. What embedding model are you using?
[01:22] Miguel: We started with an open 768-d embedding from OpenAI-community and also tried a 1536-d model for better recall on medical queries. The 1536 improves quality but increases storage and compute for ANN.
[01:35] Samir: Right, the tradeoff is classic. For hosted we can serve either dim; cost per token/embedding and storage will go up with 1536. For Dedicated you can optimize quantization and choose smaller float16/8bit configs to save storage.
[01:48] Dana: We care a lot about recall for clinical queries, false negatives are bad. But cost matters — we're evaluating. Also interested in hybrid search: BM25 to get strong lexical matches + ANN for semantic.
[01:58] Leah: Hybrid is common. One pattern we recommend: run a BM25 pass to get high-precision lexical hits, then union with ANN top-N then dedupe and rerank. That often reduces ANN false positives and keeps p95 down.
[02:12] Miguel: Which vector DBs do you integrate with? We're using Pinecone now but we want to keep options.
[02:16] Leah: We integrate work with Pinecone, Weaviate, and direct FAISS/HNSW deployments. For Dedicated we can co-locate FAISS on the same cluster and run optimized kernels. For Hosted we often run our own ANN tier and provide an API so you don't manage the DB.
[02:31] Miguel: How do you handle HNSW vs IVF/OPQ tradeoffs for 14M vectors?
[02:36] Leah: HNSW is great for recall and low-latency at moderate scale, but index memory can be larger. IVF+OPQ with PQ quantization reduces storage and can be better at higher scales. On Dedicated you can tune opq/pq settings; on Hosted we provide recommended presets. We also support approximate search and re-ranking to keep latency low.
[02:53] Priya: On the security side, can you describe data residency and encryption at rest/in transit? Also KMS/HSM support?
[02:59] Samir: Yes — we have encryption in transit TLS and at rest. For Private deployments we can integrate with customer KMS or HSM; Dedicated customers get a dedicated VPC and optional Bring-Your-Own-KMS. We are SOC2 Type II compliant; I'll share the pack.
[03:13] Priya: Do you keep embeddings or PII? For hosted, are embeddings persisted?
[03:18] Leah: By default hosted persists embeddings for index serving; retention is configurable, and we can support ephemeral embeddings for some flows. For PHI-heavy customers typically they prefer Dedicated or Private so data doesn't leave their network.
[03:29] Dana: Good to know. For our POC we prefer Dedicated or Private but want pricing for both to compare.
[03:35] Samir: Makes sense. We'll send a hosted vs dedicated vs private cost comparison. Usually Dedicated is the sweet spot if you need predictable throughput and isolation; Private is heavier lift but needed for strict compliance.
[03:47] Miguel: On throughput — how do you handle batching for embedding and retrieval? Our search path: compute query embedding (100ms), ANN search, gather top 200, cross-encoder rerank. The cross-encoder is expensive. Can Redwood run rerank on GPU with batching?
[04:02] Leah: Yes — we run cross-encoder rerank on GPU. For Dedicated you can reserve GPU capacity for rerank and we support batching across concurrent requests to maximize throughput. For Hosted we have autoscaling GPU pools but there can be cold-starts; we recommend provisioning reserved capacity for consistent p95.
[04:16] Miguel: What's the typical p95 for ANN retrieval at 14M vectors?
[04:20] Leah: With HNSW and optimized kernels you can get p95 in 10s of ms for single-query ANN on a dedicated node; end-to-end depends on your network and prep. If you include query embedding time and a small cross-encoder rerank, p95 around 150-300ms is achievable with dedicated capacity. Hosted with burst can be a little higher unless you reserve.
[04:39] Dana: Okay. Also curious about dimensionality: is 1536 worth the extra cost? Any suggestions for quantizing 1536 down?
[04:46] Leah: Sometimes 1536 gives better med/recall, particularly for medical terms. But you can reduce footprint via OPQ + PQ to 8 bytes per vector or use distillation to 768-d models. We recommend running an ablation with 1k-5k benchmark queries to measure recall@k and latency impacts. We'll share templates.
[05:03] Miguel: For reranking, we plan to do dense retrieve -> top200 -> cross-encoder. We need to limit cross-encoder to at most 50 per query to meet latency. How to choose topK?
[05:13] Leah: That's an empirical knob. Start with top200 dense, then quickly filter with BM25/hybrid, then run cross-encoder on top50. For some queries you can lower to top20 and keep high MRR. We'll help set up evals for recall/precision tradeoffs.
[05:26] Priya: On auditing, do you provide per-request logs and redaction controls? We need audit trails for access and the ability to show that PHI is isolated.
[05:36] Samir: Yes — Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and we have audit logs that include request metadata. For Private deployments logs can be pushed to customer SIEM. Redaction configs are available for logs.
[05:49] Dana: Good. Can you run an initial benchmark for us? We have 2 datasets: internal patient-note subset (~2M docs) and external literature (~10M docs). We'd like 10k queries across both.
[05:59] Leah: Absolutely. For the POC we typically run 10k queries with a mix of real queries, measure recall@10/50, latency p50/p95, and cost per query. We'll need sample queries + expected labels.
[06:11] Miguel: What's the POC timeframe? We want something quick, ideally 3 weeks to demonstrate feasibility.
[06:15] Samir: We can do a 3-week POC: week 1 prep and dataset ingest, week 2 benchmark runs and tuning, week 3 results and handoff.
[06:24] Dana: Sounds good. A few small clarifications: do you support hybrid search stacks where we keep an Elastic index for BM25 and call Redwood ANN for semantic?
[06:33] Leah: Yes, that's common. You can run BM25 in Elastic, then call Redwood ANN as a microservice to get top-N vectors, merge results, and then call Redwood rerank or run your own cross-encoder. Integration is just API calls.
[06:45] Miguel: Any guidance on vector dimensions and storage sizing? For 14M x 1536 float32 that's large — how do you typically size storage?
[06:53] Leah: Float32 is heavy; we recommend quantization for cost. Example: float32 1536-d is ~24KB per vector, uncompressed that's big. With PQ/OPQ you can get down to ~8 bytes per vector on disk in some settings. For Dedicated we can recommend node types and NVMe sizing. We'll include sizing in the benchmark runbook.
[07:11] Priya: For compliance, what's the SLA for data deletion? And do you keep backups?
[07:16] Samir: We support configurable retention and deletions. Backups are available for Dedicated/Private per contract. For hosted we have retention defaults but can set stricter policies for enterprise contracts. I'll include deletion policies in the security pack.
[07:30] Dana: Any gotchas with medical terminology and embeddings?
[07:34] Leah: Domain-specific tokens help; sometimes fine-tuning or using a domain-specific encoder helps more than just increasing dimension. Also consider boosting term matches in hybrid search for known medical terms. We'll help tune that during POC.
[07:47] Miguel: One more question — do you support approximate topK caching or prefix KV caching? We have many repeated queries.
[07:54] Leah: Yes, Redwood supports KV/prefix caching for common queries which can cut cost/latency. For rerank, caching the ANN top results can also speed things up. There was also some internal naming — sometimes our runtime docs say 'KV cash' in transcriptions, uhm sorry — 'KV cache', ha.
[08:10] (brief laughter)
[08:13] Samir: Perfect. Let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[08:16] Samir: Action items: Samir send pricing and Hosted/Dedicated/Private comparison; Leah share benchmark runbook, embedding dim guidance, and HNSW/FAISS tuning; Priya will share compliance items; Miguel confirm dataset samples. We'll target a POC kickoff week of 2025-06-23.
[08:34] Dana: That works for us. Thanks everyone.
[08:38] Miguel: Thanks.
[08:39] Priya: Bye.
[08:40] Samir: Thanks, bye.
